content: Before using palonosetron, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other anti-nausea serotonin blockers (such as ondansetron or granisetron), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. The risk of serotonin syndrome or toxicity increases if you are also taking other drugs that elevate serotonin levels. Examples include street drugs like MDMA (ecstasy), St. John’s wort, and certain antidepressants such as SSRIs (e.g., fluoxetine, paroxetine) or SNRIs (e.g., duloxetine, venlafaxine). If someone overdoses and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly for a new dosing schedule. This medication is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by cancer treatments (chemotherapy) or after surgery. It is administered by injection into a vein by a healthcare professional. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. Common side effects may include pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site, as well as headache, constipation, or diarrhea. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may increase serotonin levels and lead to a serious condition called serotonin syndrome or toxicity. The risk is higher if you are taking other drugs that increase serotonin levels, so inform your doctor or pharmacist about all the medications you are using. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing, seek medical attention immediately. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
